title: The Poor Man and His Friend in Need
summary: In Baghdad lived three devoted friends who had sworn a sacred bond of brotherhood in their youth. One was a bookbinder, the second a leather-worker, and the third a scribe. Each...
keywords: the poor man and his friend in need
full_text:
In Baghdad lived three devoted friends who had sworn a sacred bond of brotherhood in their youth. One was a bookbinder, the second a leather-worker, and the third a scribe. Each earned a modest living, and whenever one lacked bread, the others shared their earnings without keeping account.

One difficult year, the bookbinder was struck by severe misfortune: his workshop caught fire, destroying his tools and leather skins. Deeply indebted and having nothing to feed his children, he went to the leather-worker and confided his plight with tears.

The leather-worker had only one heavy purse containing a thousand silver dirhams, which he had saved over ten years to purchase new machinery. Without a moment's hesitation, the leather-worker placed the purse in his friend’s hands: 'Take this, brother! My machinery can wait; your children must not hunger.'

The bookbinder thanked him with tears of gratitude and returned home. But no sooner had he crossed his threshold than the third friend, the scribe, arrived at his door, pale and trembling. The scribe’s house had been seized by an oppressive landlord, and his family sat in the street.

The bookbinder looked at the purse of a thousand dirhams. Though he needed the money desperately himself, he thought: 'My friend's family is on the cobblestones; my children at least have a roof.' He handed the sealed purse directly to the scribe!

The scribe took the purse and ran immediately to the leather-worker to pay off his debt—for it was the leather-worker who had leased him his house!

When the leather-worker saw his own sealed purse returned to him, he was astonished. He summoned the bookbinder and the scribe, and the three friends stood together, each having placed the other's need before his own, the purse having traveled in a complete circle of selfless love!

The Caliph Harun al-Rashid, hearing of this sublime contest of selflessness, summoned the three friends, rewarded each with three thousand dinars from the royal treasury, and praised their brotherhood as the highest glory of Baghdad.
moral: True friendship puts the need of the companion above one's own comfort, creating an unbroken chain of love.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Poor Man and His Friend in Need"?
options: Loyal friendship and mutual trust overcome the greatest hardships.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
